desired: A working /wrap that turns a Claude Code session into a replayable map, structured so that Codex and Cursor can be added, with tests.
actual: v0.2 shipped as a package with three adapters, a prompt-pragmatics layer, config, hooks, skills and tests. Only the Claude Code adapter was verified on real data.
verdict: The version reached its core: a Claude Code session can be wrapped into a replay, and the package is laid out so that adding an agent is one file. It fell short on the part of 'agent-agnostic' that matters in use: the Codex and Cursor adapters were written from documentation and synthetic fixtures and never ran on real history (session ca61170e m9, m11). Whether the prompt-reading layer reads prompts accurately beyond one session is unclear from the record.

got_you_there.what: Four decisions in one message after a 19-minute pause
got_you_there.why: The agent could order the whole build around the replay without a clarification round; the build phase started in the same minute.

got_you_there.what: Reading Claude Code's on-disk format before writing anything
got_you_there.why: Capture needed no new infrastructure, so v1 was a reader plus a renderer and took about four minutes of build.

got_you_there.what: Smoke-testing the generated brief on the live session before calling it done
got_you_there.why: Surfaced three misreads (HEAD as a branch, 'version' read as config, an intent tie-break) that would otherwise have shipped.

cost_you.what: The rebuild request carried eight capabilities and a quality adjective but no done-condition; the first attempt was restarted at a higher effort level.
Preview of the replay blocked by the browser pane refusing file:// URLs; worked around by serving over localhost.
56 minutes between v1 delivery and the rebuild request. The record does not say whether this was thinking time or time elsewhere.

carried_forward.what: Codex CLI and Cursor adapters that have never parsed real history.
carried_forward.risk: The first real user of either agent will hit format drift, and the adapters will need rework under time pressure. The README says so; the code does not.

carried_forward.what: A package layout chosen by the agent under a prompt with no acceptance criteria.
carried_forward.risk: adapters / lang / digest / brief / recap / render reflects the agent's defaults, not stated requirements. Later constraints (team maps, a hosted store) may fight the split between store and render.

carried_forward.what: Python 3.9 as the floor, chosen from the machine the agent found, not from the users.
carried_forward.risk: Rules out newer syntax and stdlib features; cheap now, a constraint if the package grows.

prompting.pattern: Batches decisions after stepping away, rather than iterating in chat.
prompting.effect: Compressed the decide phase to one message; the agent never had to ask twice.

prompting.pattern: Large-scope requests with quality adjectives ('advanced enough to capture nuances') and no acceptance criteria.
prompting.effect: The agent defined what done meant; one restart followed, and the architecture is the agent's.
The product thesis and the killer moment were set by two corrections in the first twenty minutes; nothing below that level was ever corrected.

next_time: Write the acceptance list before a rebuild-sized prompt; it becomes the test list (m8).
Do not call an adapter done until it has parsed real history from that agent, or mark it unverified in the code as well as the README (m9).
Keep the live-session smoke test as the last step of every version; it is where the real bugs surfaced (m11).
